questions.prompt: Match each mixture to the best separation method.
questions.explain: Each method uses a different property: visibility, weight, size, magnetism, solubility.

questions.prompt: Match each method to the PROPERTY it uses.

pairs.right: One part is an insoluble solid
A solid is dissolved in a liquid

questions.explain: Choosing a method always starts with finding the property that differs.

questions.prompt: When muddy water is filtered, the sand left on the filter paper is called the…
questions.explain: Residue = solid left on the filter paper. Filtrate = liquid that passes through.

questions.prompt: Why can't you separate salt from salt water by filtering?
options: Dissolved salt particles are small enough to pass through the filter paper
Filter paper dissolves in salt water
questions.explain: Dissolved particles pass through filter paper with the water, so the filtrate is still salty.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to separate a mixture of SAND, SALT and IRON FILINGS.
steps: Use a magnet to remove the iron filings
Add water and stir to dissolve the salt
Evaporate the filtrate to get the salt
questions.explain: Magnet (magnetism) → dissolve (solubility) → filter (insoluble solid) → evaporate (dissolved solid).

questions.prompt: Butter is separated from curd by…
questions.explain: Churning makes the lighter fat (butter) collect and separate from the buttermilk.

questions.prompt: Letting muddy water stand so the mud sinks, then pouring off the water, is called…
questions.explain: Sedimentation = heavy particles settle. Decantation = pouring off the liquid above.

questions.prompt: Which mixtures can be separated by FILTRATION? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Filtration works only for insoluble solids. Sugar and salt dissolve, so they pass through.

questions.text: In salt pans, salt is obtained from sea water by ___ , using the heat of the ___ .
questions.explain: The sun's heat evaporates the water and leaves salt behind.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would separate a mixture of sawdust, salt and iron nails. Name the property used at each step.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Use a magnet to pull out the iron nails (magnetism). 2) Add water and stir: the salt dissolves and the sawdust floats (solubility). 3) Filter to collect the sawdust as the residue (insoluble solid). 4) Evaporate the filtrate to get the salt back (dissolved solid left when water evaporates).
rubric: I used a magnet for the nails
I dissolved the salt in water and filtered out the sawdust
I evaporated the solution to get the salt
I named a property for each step
questions.explain: Good plans name the property behind every step.
